title: Beyond Public Access in LLM Pre-Training Data
abstract: arXiv:2505.00020v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Using a legally obtained dataset of 34 copyrighted O'Reilly Media books (13,962 paragraphs), we apply the DE-COP membership inference attack to test whether OpenAI models show recognition of non-public (pay-walled) content they were not licensed to train on. Our main contribution is examining non-public books, which allows us to consider potential access violations and not just training inclusion. Our results suggest that GPT-4o, OpenAI's more recent and capable model in our sample, exhibits patterns consistent with recognition of non-public books, with an AUROC score of 0.82 (95% bootstrapped CI: 0.60-0.96) -- where above 50% is better than random chance. GPT-3.5 Turbo (trained two years prior) and the smaller GPT-4o Mini both score near chance recognition on non-public data (0.54 and 0.56, respectively). tldr: 研究者利用DE-COP成员推断攻击检测版权书籍内容，发现GPT-4o表现出对其未获授权训练的非公开付费内容的识别能力（AUROC达0.82），这暗示可能存在超越“训练数据包含”之外的数据访问违规行为。
